title: World of Warcraft
japaneseTitle: ワールド オブ ウォークラフト
director: Rob Pardo, Jeff Kaplan, Tom Chilton
designer: Jeff Kaplan, Tom Chilton, Allen Adham
composer: Jason Hayes, Tracy W. Bush, Derek Duke, Glenn Stafford
shortDescription: Blizzard's global cultural phenomenon that democratized MMORPGs and welcomed over 12 million subscribers to Azeroth.
historicalSignificance: The defining MMORPG in human history, discarding the brutal death penalties of early online games in favor of quest-driven progression, accessible instanced raiding, and rich social guild infrastructure that peaked at over 12 million active monthly subscribers.

editorialContent.overview: Launched by Blizzard Entertainment on the tenth anniversary of the Warcraft franchise in November 2004, World of Warcraft (WoW) transformed massively multiplayer online role-playing games from a niche hobby into an unprecedented global mainstream cultural phenomenon. Setting foot in Azeroth, players joined either the Alliance or the Horde across the continents of Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms.
editorialContent.gameplay: Players progress from humble beginnings killing boars outside Goldshire or Durotar up to 40-player endgame raids in Molten Core, Blackwing Lair, and Ahn'Qiraj. Seamless quest-driven leveling replaced mindless mob grinding, complemented by deep trade skills (Blacksmithing, Alchemy, Engineering) and world PvP warfare across Southshore and Stranglethorn Vale.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Blizzard engineered an extraordinary seamless zone-streaming engine without loading screens between territories, supported by an open Lua/XML user-interface scripting API that enabled an expansive ecosystem of community add-ons.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: World of Warcraft dominated 2000s internet culture, featured in an Emmy-winning South Park episode ('Make Love, Not Warcraft'), birthing the Leroy Jenkins meme, and uniting millions of players across countries and languages into lifelong friendships and marriages.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved in active continuity on Blizzard's servers for over two decades, alongside the authentic recreation project World of Warcraft: Classic launched in 2019.

verifiedFactualData.sales: Over 12 million active concurrent monthly subscribers at its peak; billions in lifetime gross revenue
